verses.text: Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Have you watched a doe give birth to her fawns?
Can you count the months they carry their young? Do you know when they’ll give birth?
They crouch down, deliver their young, and their labor pains end.
Their young grow strong in the open country. They go out on their own and never return.
Who let the wild donkey go free? Who untied the ropes of that swift donkey?
I gave him the wilderness for a home and the salt flats as a place to live.
He laughs at the noise of the city and never hears a driver shouting at him.
The mountains are his pasture, and he searches for every green thing he can find.
Will the wild ox agree to work for you? Will it spend the night by your feeding trough?
Can you harness it to plow a straight furrow? Will it follow you and till the valleys?
Will you trust it because it’s so strong and leave it to do your work?
Can you count on it to bring in what you’ve sown and gather grain at your threshing floor?
The ostrich flaps her wings proudly, but do those feathers show any tenderness?
She leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the dust.
She forgets that a foot could crush them or that a wild animal could trample them.
She treats her young harshly, as though they weren’t hers. She doesn’t worry that her labor might go to waste,
because God withheld wisdom from her and gave her no understanding.
But when she rises to run, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
Did you give the horse its strength? Did you dress its neck with a rippling mane?
Did you teach it to leap like a locust? Its mighty snort fills people with awe.
It paws the ground in the valley, eager to use its strength, and charges toward armed men.
It laughs at fear and doesn’t flinch or turn away from the sword.
The quiver rattles at its side along with the flashing spear and javelin.
It tears across the ground in a fury and won’t stand still when the trumpet sounds.
At each blast it snorts, ‘Aha!’ It smells battle far away and hears the commanders thundering and the soldiers shouting.
Is it your wisdom that makes the hawk soar and spread its wings toward the south?
Does the eagle rise at your command and build its nest high above the ground?
It lives on the cliff and makes its home on a rocky ledge, safe in its stronghold.
From there it watches for prey, spotting it from far away.
Its young drink blood. Wherever the dead lie, the eagle is there.
